newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - January 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - January 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan has expressed concern at the growing military cooperation between Israel and India.

- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid has said the International Monetary Fund agreed to release the stalled tranche only after his government dispelled the impression that the deposed government of Benazir Bhutto was being restored.
- The caretaker government is to reduce Pakistan's debt to $15 to $20 billion from the present level of $55 billion, said Salman Shah, chairman of the Privatisation Commssion.

- A foreign office spokesman has indicated that formal recognition of the Taleban government was imminent because ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani's regime had run out its mandate and was driven out of the Afghan capital.
- The caretaker government, in a bid to build an impression of impartial accountability, has decided to arrest big defaulters and corrupt politicians and bureaucrats.
- The World Bank has expressed its concern over politicisation of decision-making, lack of accountability and little transparancy in the financial matters.

- Local and foreign shipping companies operating from Karachi Port and nearby Port Qasim have decided to impose base adjustment factor at the rate of nine percent on all imports and exports effective January 1.
